records.reason: TypeSignalsInteractor validates and propagates TrackId while orchestrating per-layer execution; it neither computes crate-source/lockfile/toolchain hashes nor decides extraction reuse. IN-05's implementation-input hashing and extraction-skip behavior belongs to the executor adapter surface, which is separately verified.

TypeSignalsInteractor carries the validated TrackId through layer evaluation and enforces active-track consistency; its request contract contains no spec input. Spec-text change detection and catalogue-to-spec signal re-evaluation belong to the catalogue↔spec evaluation surface, not this interactor's declared surface.

TypeSignalsInteractor's declared surface is track validation and per-layer orchestration: new(layer_bindings, executor) and a run that forwards each resolved layer binding to the executor. Comparing recorded hashes and deciding whether rustdoc extraction is skipped happens behind the executor port it calls, so AC-05's skip conditions are not expressible through this entry's declaration; they are verified at the executor adapter and composition surfaces.

TypeSignalsInteractor receives no catalogue or spec input; it only carries a validated track and resolved layer binding to the executor. The catalogue/spec-only re-evaluation without rustdoc extraction belongs to the catalogue-to-spec and executor surfaces, not this interactor's declared surface.

FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter's observable API accepts only an already constructed ProviderSessionCacheKey for load, save, and remove. A dispatch whose target artifact set is undetermined never yields such a key, so the bypass the anchor promises happens before any call can reach this adapter and cannot be expressed or observed through its surface. The partitioning behavior the adapter does own is covered by its key-isolation tests.
ProviderSessionCachePort stores opaque entries and reports lookup results; it neither resolves profiles nor chooses reuse versus a new reviewer session.
ProviderSessionCachePort exposes keyed cache CRUD only; deciding whether capability work continues in a resumed or new provider session is outside this port's declared surface.

ProviderSessionCachePort returns stored entries or storage errors but does not launch reviewer rounds; selecting a new session after a mismatch, failure, or expiry is consumer control flow outside the port.

ProviderSessionCachePort's declared surface is exactly three keyed-storage methods — load(&ProviderSessionCacheKey) -> Result<Option<ProviderSessionCacheEntry>, ProviderSessionCacheError>, save(&key, &entry), and remove(&key). No method receives a resolved profile, compares provider or model values, or dispatches a session, so mismatch rejection and fresh-session dispatch are not expressible through this trait's signatures. The port's whole contribution to the anchor is faithfully preserving the entry that carries the provider/model binding data for the caller's comparison, and that preservation is what its conformance tests exercise.
ProviderSessionCachePort has no reviewer invocation, flag, file-list, or diff operation; reviewer resume and re-evaluation behavior is not representable by this cache interface.
FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter implements filesystem cache persistence and retrieval; it does not select or execute reviewer rounds, while its storage behavior remains directly testable.
FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter reads and writes persisted entries but has no profile-resolution or provider-dispatch operation that could choose a new reviewer session.
FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter is a keyed filesystem store; deciding whether capability work is resumed or started anew is outside its declared adapter surface.

FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter implements cache CRUD, path selection, codec handling, and symlink rejection; starting a new reviewer session after a mismatch, failure, or expiry is consumer control flow outside this adapter.
FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter persists keyed entries without resolving profiles or dispatching providers; stale-session fallback is outside this adapter's storage surface.

FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter has no provider invocation, reviewer prompt, flag, file-list, or diff operation; reviewer resume and full-scope re-evaluation are outside this adapter's declared surface.
CapabilityProfile is an immutable resolved-value carrier; CN-02's resume-time profile resolution and per-run execution-flag re-injection are dispatch-path behavior outside this entry's surface.
ReasoningEffort is a closed-vocabulary value type; CN-02's resume-time profile resolution and per-run execution-flag re-injection are dispatch-path behavior outside this entry's surface.

Sha256DigestError declares the digest validation failure vocabulary (InvalidLength, InvalidHex) surfaced by Sha256Digest::try_new. Recording declaration and implementation-input hashes in the per-layer artifact and comparing them for freshness happen on the document codec and evaluator surfaces; no method of this error enum can record, load, or compare an artifact, so the anchor promise is not expressible here.

TypeSignalsSchemaVersion is a validated non-zero version value exposed through try_new and value accessors. It cannot record hashes into an artifact or perform freshness comparison; those behaviors live on the type-signals document and codec surfaces where they are separately verified.

TypeSignalsSchemaVersionError only names the rejection of a zero schema version raised by TypeSignalsSchemaVersion::try_new. Recording freshness hashes and refusing to reuse incomplete artifacts are document codec and evaluator behaviors that no variant of this error can express or observe.

TypeSignalsError only transports execution failures after the per-layer freshness decision; it cannot establish the all-input comparison or skip invariant owned by the evaluator and reuse-decision entries.

TypeSignalsError is an error-transport type and has no snapshot-read, parse, hash-validation, or reuse-decision surface; those behaviors are owned by RustdocSchemaExporter and TypeSignalsReuseDecision.
TypeSignalsError reports a failed command but does not persist schema-versioned freshness identities or select conservative recomputation; artifact and evaluator entries own that behavior.
TypeSignalsRequest carries command inputs and layer selection but neither stores current freshness identities nor makes the per-layer reuse decision required by this invariant.
TypeSignalsRequest does not resolve or normalize Cargo build-input closures; that layer-granular responsibility belongs to the infrastructure build-input evaluator.
LoadCatalogueSpecSignalsForViewError is a fail-closed catalogue-spec signal-loading error representation; it carries no per-layer input matching or skip decision behavior required by IN-05.

LoadCatalogueSpecSignalsForViewError represents only failed catalogue-spec signal loading and exposes no extraction or rerun-decision operation. A successful matching input never produces this error, so this declaration cannot select reevaluation without rustdoc or re-extraction.

ProviderSessionCacheEntry is an immutable persisted payload with accessors only. It neither looks up cache entries nor invokes a provider, so provider/model mismatch, expiry, resume failure, and new-session fallback are not observable behavior of this declaration.

ProviderSessionCacheEntry is an immutable, private-field payload with accessors only; it has no provider invocation, sandbox, or execution-flag API. The port preserves the resolved profile values, while explicit resume-time flag injection is outside this declaration's representable behavior.

ProviderSessionCacheEntry is an immutable persisted payload with accessors only; it exposes no cache-lookup or provider-execution operation. New-session fallback is therefore not an observable behavior of this declaration; the port reports unreadable entries without yielding a session.

ProviderSessionCacheEntry is an immutable record of a stored session: an id plus the provider, model, and effort it was created under, exposed through read accessors only. It performs no dispatch, so falling back to a new session or re-injecting execution flags cannot be represented or observed on this value's surface; the entry's contribution is faithfully carrying the data those decisions read.
